about: Template sanity parity cases (shared-1.9.0). Loaded by meshDeckShared's TemplateSanityParityTests and by the catalogue CI's check-catalog.py self-test, so the Swift and Python rules stay identical. Each case's template is the base below with these fields replaced. refused: whether the template must be hidden (Swift: TemplateSanity.problems is non-empty; CI: catalog_sanity.problems is non-empty or catalog_risk would refuse a host-file word). key: the refused compose key Swift reports, when one.

cases.name: use_api_socket key
cases.compose:
services:
  app:
    image: x
    use_api_socket: true

cases.name: build block with a remote context
build carried in from an anchor
quoted build in a flow value
build as a label key (anywhere, as shipped meshDeck 1.0.3 refuses it)
cases.compose:
services:
  app:
    image: x
    labels:
      build: "1"

cases.name: provider as a lowercase environment key
cases.compose:
services:
  app:
    image: x
    environment:
      provider: x

cases.name: host-side words that are not keys
host-side words only in a variable's help
cases.compose:
services:
  app:
    image: x
    environment:
      VPN: ${VPN}

variables.label: VPN key
variables.help: The provider's key, from your build page; no env_file needed

cases.name: env_file as plain text in a compose comment
cases.compose:
services:
  app:
    image: x # no env_file here

cases.name: embedded config is not compose
cases.compose:
services: {}
configs:
  c:
    content: |
      include: x
